purpose: LLM adversarial refactoring framework - final optimization after self-application
context: Self-optimized: removed execution_modes duplication, consolidated settings, maintained functionality

user_environment.pub2: 45% Ruby, 45% Shell, 10% HTML - main mixed repo

questions: Is this the simplest working solution?
What would Rails do? (convention over configuration)
Are we solving the right problem?

reasoning.dry: Find duplication: similar code blocks, repeated patterns
reasoning.kiss: Find complexity: deep nesting, long methods
reasoning.solid: Find violations: multiple responsibilities, poor interfaces
reasoning.yagni: Find unused: grep for references, remove dead code

rationale.adversarial_validation: Plateau achieved through hostile questioning, polite LLMs don't challenge enough
rationale.ask_dont_guess: Critical breakthrough - stack detection failed, asking users works
rationale.preservation_absolute: LLMs love to 'improve' working code and truncate output, causing regressions
rationale.multiple_perspectives: Single perspective misses issues, consensus prevents groupthink
rationale.cross_reference_critical: Finds dead code that looks important but has no callers
rationale.anti_patterns: Don't guess stack, compliance theater fails, over-engineering backfires, single perspective misses issues
rationale.meta_removal: Self-validation happens through execution, not documentation storage
rationale.safety_integration: Circuit breakers prevent infinite loops and resource exhaustion
rationale.self_optimization: Framework applied to itself, removed execution_modes duplication, consolidated settings
